metadata.title: Stocktwits AI Roundup: Meta’s Capex, Lam’s Supply Warning Hit Tech Stocks As Netflix Disappoints

content.text:
-
Meta raised the low end of its capital expenditure forecast for the year.
-
Western Digital and Lam Research beat earnings expectations, pointing to strong AI storage and chip-equipment demand.
-
Netflix shares slid on a weak profit outlook.
Tech heavyweights Netflix (NFLX), Meta Platforms (META) and Western Digital (WDC) delivered mixed results this week as the earnings season enters its most critical stretch. While revenue and profits have grown, investors are increasingly scrutinizing the mounting costs of expansion, data center investments and AI development.
Technology stocks fell sharply on Thursday; investors will now turn to next week's reports from tech stalwarts Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Intel for fresh clues.
Here's a roundup of key stories from the past week:
Tech Selloff Deepens
Tech stocks suffered a sharp sell-off on Thursday amid renewed concerns about risks tied to the AI investment boom, mainly whether massive AI investments would generate sufficient returns.
The Nasdaq declined 2.6%, its steepest daily decline since June, while the S&P 500 dropped 1.2%. Meta tumbled 7%, Nvidia (NVDA) lost 4%, and SpaceX (SPCX) fell about 9%. Meta's higher capex floor, among other things, triggered the selloff.
Meta Posts Strong Q3 But AI Spending Plan Triggers Selloff
Meta reported better-than-expected Q3 revenue and issued strong guidance for the current quarter. However, another increase in its annual spending forecast and plans for a new share structure worried investors, sending the stock down 7% on Thursday.
Meta increased the lower end of its capex forecast range by $5 billion, to a range of $135 billion to $145 billion.
Western Digital, Lam Research Beat Expectations
Western Digital reported Q1 revenue and profit above expectations, forecast current-quarter revenue ahead of estimates, and raised its dividend, underscoring exceptionally robust storage demand.
CEO Irving Tan said demand is increasingly coming from customers outside its core base, including neoclouds and AI frontier labs.
Lam Research (LRCX) also reported Q1 revenue and profit above expectations. However, WDC shares fell 6.4% the day after its report, while Lam Research shares also declined as investors rotated out of AI-linked stocks on Thursday.
Netflix, Super Micro Deliver Contrasting Signals
Netflix shares slid after its Q4 profit forecast fell short of Wall Street expectations and the company cut its full-year advertising forecast. Third-quarter revenue rose nearly 12%, in line with Wall Street targets, but at the slowest rate of increase in nearly three years.
